Record Class SlotStateChannel<T>

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.state.SlotStateChannel<T>
public record SlotStateChannel<T>(net.minecraft.resources.Identifier id, com.mojang.serialization.Codec<T> codec, net.minecraft.network.codec.StreamCodec<net.minecraft.network.RegistryFriendlyByteBuf, T> streamCodec, T defaultValue, SlotStateChannel.Visibility visibility, SlotStateChannel.CanWrite canWrite, com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.ModeScope scope) extends Record
A typed per-slot state channel, the handle consumers use to read and write slot state. Created with SlotState.register(Identifier, Codec, StreamCodec, Object) (PRIVATE) or SlotState.register(Identifier, Codec, StreamCodec, Object, Visibility).

A channel has two codecs. codec is for persistence and encodes to NBT through NbtOps.INSTANCE, so stored values are readable with vanilla's /data get. streamCodec is the compact binary form sent over the network.

State lives in the open menu; behavior does not

The Address methods here (get(Address), set(Address, Object) and their explicit-viewer versions) work differently from how slot behavior is set up, on purpose:
  • Behavior (gating, binding, mending, quick-move) is declared by address at init and applies as soon as a slot with that address appears. It lives in the engine, independent of any open menu.
  • State read or written by address resolves against the viewer's currently open menu. If the address names no live slot in that menu, a read returns defaultValue and a write does nothing. There is no address-based path for init-time or menu-free state.

For menu-free state, server automation, or a created slot's state at init time, use the persistent-key overloads instead. They name storage directly, with no open menu and no live slot:

  • get(Player, PersistentContainerKey, int) and set(Player, PersistentContainerKey, int, Object): player-, block entity- or entity-scoped state through a PersistentContainerKey and a container-slot index (server only).
  • get(Container, int): a SHARED value at a placed container by index, with no viewer, for hopper or dropper automation.

In short, use addresses for behavior and for state in an open menu, and the persistent keys whenever there is no open menu to resolve against.

Mode scope

A channel is in effect in its scope(): while the viewing player's mode is outside it, reads give defaultValue and a client's writes are neither shown nor sent (the server refuses them too). Stored values are kept, and show again when the mode comes back. Writes made by server code are stored whatever the mode. A read with no viewing player (server code with no player at hand, a hopper seam) has no mode to be in, so a SURVIVAL or CREATIVE channel reads its default there; pass the player, or use a BOTH channel for state automation reads.

  • Method Details

    • get

      public T get(Address address)
      Reads this channel's value at the slot named by address, in the client player's currently open menu. Same as get(Slot), but the slot is named by Address instead of a live Slot. Returns defaultValue when the address names no live slot in the open menu (see SlotState.readByAddress). Use get(Player, Address) for an explicit viewer, for example on the server.

    • get

      public T get(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, Address address)
      Reads this channel's value at the slot named by address for an explicit player, resolving the slot in that player's open menu. The address version of get(Player, Slot).

    • set

      public void set(Address address, T value)
      Writes value at the slot named by address, in the client player's open menu. The address version of set(Slot, Object). Does nothing when the address names no live slot in the open menu.

    • set

      public void set(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, Address address, T value)

    • get

      public T get(net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot slot)
      Reads this channel's value at slot. Works on both sides when the slot belongs to a player-scoped container (Inventory, PlayerEnderChestContainer). On the server, a block-entity or entity slot with no player to resolve returns defaultValue; pass the player with get(Player, Slot). A creative slot wrapper is seen through.

    • get

      public T get(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot slot)
      Reads this channel's value at slot for an explicit player. Needed for server-side reads on block entity or entity containers, where private state depends on whose it is. SHARED channels ignore the player but still accept it.

    • set

      public void set(net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot slot, T value)
      Writes value at slot. See get(Slot) for how each side behaves. On the client the write goes to the server, which checks it. Writing the default removes the entry.

      Parameters:

    • get

      public T get(net.minecraft.world.Container container, int containerSlotIndex)
      Reads the SHARED value at (container, containerSlotIndex) with no Slot, open menu or viewer, for automation (hopper, dropper, dispenser) that touches a placed container directly by index. The library resolves the container internally, including composite containers, so a double chest resolves to the half that owns the slot.

      Returns defaultValue off the server, for a container that can't be resolved, or for a PRIVATE channel, since a private value belongs to a viewer and this path has none. Read only: writes still go through the owner or menu (and shared writes are broadcast). The consumer builds its own enforcement on this read, such as blocking a hopper extract; the library only reports state.
